answer: An agent marketplace requires each bidding identity to lock a fixed bond for 30 days, whether its job is to map a knoll, appraise onyx, or analyze an echo. Creating keys is free, but activating 1,000 fake bidders requires 1,000 bonds, tying up capital for the full period. If an agent signs conflicting commitments for the same job, anyone can submit both signatures to slash its bond, making that deception provably costly.
